title: Rotting Oranges
summary: Given an m x n grid where each cell contains either 0 (representing an empty cell), 1 (representing a fresh orange), or 2 (representing a rotten orange), every minute any fresh orange that is 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten orange will become rotten.
statement: Given an m x n grid where each cell contains either 0 (representing an empty cell), 1 (representing a fresh orange), or 2 (representing a rotten orange), every minute any fresh orange that is 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten orange will become rotten. Return the minimum number of minutes required until no cell contains a fresh orange. If it is impossible for all oranges to become rotten, return -1.
constraints: Zero is empty, one fresh, and two rotten; rotting spreads orthogonally each minute.
Return minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1.
hints: All initially rotten oranges spread simultaneously, so use multi-source BFS.
Queue every rotten cell at minute zero and count fresh cells.
Rot each fresh neighbor once, decrement fresh, and enqueue with minute+1.
BFS distance is earliest rot time; remaining fresh cells prove impossibility.
editorial: BFS distance is earliest rot time; remaining fresh cells prove impossibility.

tests.explanation: Layered spread reaches the last orange after four minutes.
The isolated lower-left fresh orange can never rot, so return -1.
